title: Agent-issued manual refunds with an audit trail
name: Manual refund service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code captures what changed for the audit trail? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
An agent without the bookings:refund permission calls issueRefund. What ends up in the audit store?
choices: A denied audit record, written by saveWithAudit
Nothing: the call throws before loading the booking, and no audit record is written
An audit record with before and after equal, because nothing changed
The booking's notes gain a line recording the attempt

questions.prompt: Why does the service persist the booking and the audit record through a single saveWithAudit call instead of two separate writes?
choices: So the refund and its audit record are committed together, and one cannot exist without the other
Because the audit store is faster when batched
So the audit record can be written even if the booking save fails
To avoid validating the refund amount twice

questions.prompt: A booking of 50000 cents has 30000 refunded. An agent refunds 20000. What is the resulting state?
